note: Structured record of what was decided, built and verified. Observable facts and short decision rationales only — never reasoning traces, private prompts, credentials or customer data. Unknown values stay null rather than being guessed.

events.goal: Establish what the environment can actually do before committing to an architecture.
events.decision_summary: Verified toolchain, GitHub identity and scopes, Cloudflare account and token permissions, disk space, and that verify.itisyou.app was unclaimed.
alternatives_considered: Assume the documented environment and start building
events.decision_reason: The plan explicitly warns against assuming account access. Three findings changed later decisions: the Cloudflare OAuth token carries zone:read only, the account already holds 32 unrelated Workers and 13 unrelated D1 databases, and this machine's local DNS resolver is broken so hostname checks must use DNS-over-HTTPS.
events.limitations: Cloudflare plan tier was inferred from the existing count of 13 D1 databases exceeding the free-tier limit, not read from a billing API.
events.next_step: Freeze the shared contracts before delegating.

events.goal: Freeze the vocabulary every agent shares, so twelve specialists cannot each invent their own.
events.decision_summary: The customer rule language is a closed set of typed operators over an allowlisted set of fields. Money is integer minor units with a single budget-availability formula.
alternatives_considered: A general expression language (JSONLogic, CEL, a sandboxed JS subset)
events.decision_reason: A general expression language would let a customer rule become an unbounded computation or a network request, and would make the FAILED/UNVERIFIED distinction unprovable. Integer pence removes an entire class of cap-drift bug; a decimal library would add a dependency for no benefit at this scale.
events.limitations: The operator set covers the one supported workflow shape. A second workflow shape will need a contract version bump, not an added escape hatch.

events.goal: Prove the hosting path end to end before building on it.
events.decision_summary: Two D1 databases in EU-West, staging and production Workers, custom domain verify.itisyou.app, cron on production only. Background work uses a D1 due-job table plus a one-minute cron trigger rather than Cloudflare Queues.
alternatives_considered: Durable Object ledger for budget accounting
events.decision_reason: A D1 due-job table with a partial index is deterministic, testable without network, and adds no dependency; Queues would add delivery semantics we would then have to test around. EU-West was chosen over the default ENAM for a UK business. Staging deliberately has no cron so a test environment cannot generate recurring cost.
test_evidence_refs: 0001_init.sql applied to both remote databases: 70 statements each
/health probes D1 and reports database reachable
events.limitations: The site currently serves an honest holding page. Nothing is for sale and no account can be created.

events.goal: Make a permanently public repository safe before any code that touches credentials exists.
events.decision_summary: Secret scanning and push protection enabled, private vulnerability reporting enabled, Dependabot alerts and auto-fixes enabled, a branch ruleset blocking deletion and force-push and requiring a reviewed pull request, and default workflow permissions set to read.
alternatives_considered: Start private and flip to public at release
events.decision_reason: The founder requires permanent public visibility, so every byte must be treated as permanently disclosed from the first commit. Writing .gitignore and the secret scanner before generating any credential is the only ordering that works.
test_evidence_refs: GitHub push protection blocked a push containing credential-shaped test fixtures; fixtures were rewritten rather than allowlisted
events.limitations: Repository-admin bypass on the ruleset is deliberate so the owner can push directly. External contributions require review.

events.goal: Settle the offer and write factual copy, so no agent later invents a claim.
events.decision_summary: Produced a claims-to-implementation map and cut every claim nothing implements.
events.decision_reason: Claims cut included real-time results (results depend on a one-minute poll and a deadline up to an hour), works with any CRM, we tell you the automation is broken (we observe downstream evidence, not the automation), and tenant isolation stated as a present-tense guarantee before the enforcing code existed.
events.limitations: Legal identity fields left as TODO_OWNER_INPUT. Worst-case external-call volume of 4,000 per workspace per month is an estimate pending the connector implementation.

events.goal: Make a false VERIFIED structurally impossible.
events.decision_summary: Pure, time-injected evaluator and decision table. Email normalisation deliberately does not strip +tags or dots. Only RECORD_NOT_FOUND and EVENT_NOT_OBSERVED are authoritative absences.
alternatives_considered: Treating any missing evidence at the deadline as FAILED
events.decision_reason: Verification must never widen an equivalence class: stripping a +tag would let an address the customer controls satisfy a rule about emailing the enquirer. Treating any absence as FAILED would convert our own outages into customer failures.
events.limitations: Pure logic only. It proves the decision is correct given a bundle; it does not prove the bundle was gathered correctly — that is A04's connectors.
events.next_step: Connectors must supply provider_account_id and honest origin values.

events.goal: Tenant scoping, idempotency and credential handling that hold under concurrency.
events.decision_summary: AES-GCM credential envelopes bind workspace, provider and purpose into the AAD. Source-event admission reserves the run allowance inside the same D1 batch using a CASE expression that violates NOT NULL on exhaustion, forcing a rollback.
alternatives_considered: Conditional UPDATE for the allowance guard
events.decision_reason: A conditional UPDATE inside a D1 batch cannot abort the batch — it silently reports zero changes after the inserts have already committed, which would admit an event without reserving its allowance. The NOT NULL violation is the only mechanism that rolls the whole batch back. vitest-pool-workers 0.9.14 fails to start against the hoisted miniflare; Node 22's built-in node:sqlite gave the same SQLite engine with no new dependency.
test_evidence_refs: 205 cases across API-, AUTH- and PERSIST- ranges, all passing
events.limitations: The SQLite harness exercises real SQL, real transactions and the real idempotency guards, but not Cloudflare network behaviour, D1 replicas or true OS-level parallelism.
events.next_step: Six security findings from A10 to fix.

events.goal: Challenge the implementation independently rather than confirm it.
events.decision_summary: 40+ threats with honest per-control status, 30 blocking acceptance checks, 9 explicitly accepted risks, and 156 security cases of which 6 are asserted failures against real findings.
events.decision_reason: A finding is only real when a test fails on it. The critical finding: openCredential accepted an optional expected AAD, so a lookup by connection id would decrypt any tenant's row because the stored AAD travels with the row and satisfies the GCM tag.
test_evidence_refs: 156 security cases, 150 passing, 6 failing by design
A10's independently written Stripe and Svix verifiers proved byte-compatible with A02's
events.limitations: Two independent readings of a specification agreeing is the strongest evidence available without a live provider call. It is not a live provider call.

events.goal: Make the 500-case release gate honest rather than inflated.
events.decision_summary: 578 designed cases across 12 categories, every category above its minimum, plus a checker that fails on duplicate ids, shortfalls, missing fields and identical requirement+setup pairs.
alternatives_considered: Renumbering the 449 already-implemented case ids onto the ledger
events.decision_reason: Padding detection matters more than the total. The checker was smoke-tested by deliberately corrupting a copy of the ledger; every detector produced its own specific failure.
test_evidence_refs: node scripts/verify-test-cases.mjs exits 0; --strict blocks on reconciliation
events.limitations: The ledger is a design, and 415 of its cases are not yet implemented. Implemented ids and ledger ids are currently separate namespaces; the ledger must be reconciled to reality before the gate can be claimed.

events.goal: Mount the routers behind a strict Content-Security-Policy and confirm the deployed pages are correct by looking at them.
events.decision_summary: Hash-based CSP with no unsafe-inline, computed from the same constants the page renders. One narrow concession: style-src-attr allows inline style attributes; script-src-attr is none.
events.decision_reason: The first strict policy blocked inline style attributes, so the demo page verification-rate meter fell back to full width: the number said 33% and the bar said 100%. The markup was correct throughout — only a screenshot revealed it. On a product whose thesis is that a partial result must never display as a pass, an inflated bar is the worst available defect, so the concession was taken deliberately and named in the code rather than hidden. A blanket unsafe-inline would not even have worked, since the spec ignores it while a hash is present.
test_evidence_refs: Deployed to staging and screenshotted before and after; meter renders 33% after the fix
All 13 public routes return 200 with the policy applied
events.limitations: The concession stays until the computed geometry moves to predefined classes. Responsive widths were not confirmed through this tool and are covered by the browser suite instead.
events.next_step: Remove style-src-attr once A05 converts the geometry to classes.

events.goal: Replace the holding page at verify.itisyou.app with the real public site.
events.decision_summary: Deployed the marketing site, the worked-example demo, the legal pages and the development story to production. The customer application is reachable but runs on a synthetic data port, labelled as such on every page.
alternatives_considered: Wait until the real data layer is wired before deploying anything
events.decision_reason: A holding page tells a visitor nothing. The public pages are complete and every claim on them maps to implemented behaviour, and the synthetic customer pages carry an unmissable banner plus a stripe. Shipping honest incompleteness is better than shipping nothing, and it makes the work inspectable.
test_evidence_refs: CSP and HSTS present on production responses
Bundle scanned for secrets before upload: clean
events.limitations: Nothing is for sale. No account can be created. Every page under /app returns synthetic data and says so. Live payments and provider-backed evidence both await owner credentials.
events.next_step: Wire the real D1 repositories behind the three data ports.

events.goal: Stop the tenant-scope source scan reporting customer-facing prose as unscoped SQL.
events.decision_summary: The SQL detector now requires a verb AND a clause, both uppercase, and a paired check fails the build on any lowercase SQL verb in the data layer.
alternatives_considered: Add an allowlist entry for the offending file
Reword the customer-facing copy to avoid the word update
events.decision_reason: The payment-recovery notice says you can update your card and mentions runs and evidence, which a case-insensitive keyword match read as an unscoped query on customer tables. Allowlisting the file or bending the copy around a detector both leave the detector wrong. A security check that fires on English gets muted, and a muted check protects nothing. Tightening to uppercase opens a loophole for lowercase SQL, so the two changes are a pair and neither is safe alone.
test_evidence_refs: Measured rather than assumed: across 285 string literals in the data layer the old rule detected 121 statements and the new rule detects exactly the same 121 — zero detection lost
SEC-205 added; 19 cases in the file pass
events.limitations: The scan is a structural heuristic over source text. It cannot see SQL assembled at runtime, and it is not a substitute for the behavioural tenant-isolation tests.
